meta.titre: Field Shift: crop rotations for a changing climate
meta.description: Compare crop rotations suited to the climate and soil of your plot, built on NASA Earth observation data.

climat.titre: Crop rotations built for a climate that
climat.texte: Field Shift combines NASA satellite data with the expertise of IRAD Dschang to help farmers decide what to plant, and when.
climat.legende: less rainfall in Dschang over 10 years

semis.titre: Rainfall is shifting, planting must shift
semis.texte: The start of the rainy season varies by up to 55 days from one year to the next. The tool accounts for it, crop by crop.

validation.texte: Ten years of ground measurements: GPM IMERG rainfall matches within 2%. NASA POWER, which overestimates it by 32%, is set aside.

hero.agriculteurAlt: Smiling farmer holding a basket of maize, beans, groundnuts, cassava and potatoes
hero.sources: Data: NASA GPM IMERG · NASA POWER · ISRIC SoilGrids · IRAD Dschang weather station

probleme.titre: Yesterday’s farming calendars no longer work
probleme.intro: In Dschang, rainfall is dropping, the rainy season starts earlier or later from one year to the next, and temperatures are rising. Yet farmers still plant on the same dates, with the same crop sequences.

pluie.texte: 2,181 mm per year on average in 2005-2014, versus 1,921 mm in 2015-2024.

debut.titre: days of spread in rainy-season onset
debut.texte: Depending on the year, the rains started anywhere between 22 February and 18 April. Planting too early means risking the seedlings.
debut.source: Source: NASA GPM IMERG, daily data

chaleur.texte: Extra heat that weighs on crops that like cool conditions, such as potatoes and beans.

frise.titre: Rainfall is dropping at the worst moments of the calendar

probleme.conclusion: Less water at planting and at the end of the cycle, exactly when crops are most fragile. What to plant, and when, needs rethinking.

commentCaMarche.titre: Three data sources, one safer decision
commentCaMarche.intro: Field Shift does not decide for the farmer. It puts side by side what the sky, the soil and the farmer’s own priorities say, then proposes rotations to compare.

climat.texte: Monthly rainfall over 20 years, the start of the rainy season year by year, and temperature.

sol.texte: pH, clay and organic carbon in the top 30 centimetres. Farmers can also enter their own soil test.

priorites.texte: Yield, water security, soil health: each farmer sets what matters most, from 1 to 5.

moteur.titre: Every possible rotation, scored one by one

points.0: It evaluates every possible rotation over 2 years, that is 4 growing seasons.
points.1: For each crop, it checks water over the whole cycle and at planting, temperature and pH.
points.2: It applies IRAD’s rules: forbidden sequences, return intervals, seasons to avoid.
points.3: It gives three scores out of 100: yield, water security and soil health.

resultat.texte: The best options for the chosen priorities, each with its reasons and IRAD’s practical advice.
resultat.aria: Example: the 3 rotations proposed for the IRAD Dschang plot

commentCaMarche.cta: Try it on the IRAD plot

validation.titre: Satellite data, checked on the ground
validation.intro: Before trusting satellites, we tested them against ten years of records from IRAD’s weather station in Dschang. The result: GPM IMERG matches the ground truth, NASA POWER does not. So the tool uses IMERG for rainfall.
validation.photoAlt: Entrance sign of IRAD’s multipurpose agricultural research station in Dschang
validation.photoLegende: IRAD station in Dschang, where we obtained the rainfall records (2014-2024).

imerg.verdict: It follows the dry and wet months just like the station, and the rainfall total is almost exact.

power.verdict: It overestimates rainfall by a third. We only use it for temperature.

graphique.titre: Annual rainfall: the station vs the satellites
graphique.moyennes: Average: station 1,978 mm, IMERG 1,928 mm, POWER 2,600 mm
graphique.aria: Bar chart of annual rainfall from 2014 to 2024: IRAD station, GPM IMERG and NASA POWER. IMERG stays close to the station, POWER often far exceeds it.
graphique.note: Comparison over 118 months. 2018 is missing from the station records; 2 inconsistent months were excluded.

validation.saisons: Season by season, IMERG stays within 3% of the station: 988 mm vs 1,019 mm in the 1st season, 885 mm vs 910 mm in the 2nd season. And rainfall per season is precisely what the engine uses to score crops.

irad.titre: Built with the researchers of IRAD Dschang
irad.intro: Satellites tell us when it rains. IRAD’s researchers know what each crop can tolerate and what wears a soil out. We went to see them at the station, and their rules are built directly into the engine.

regle.texte: Alternate a crop that enriches the soil with nitrogen and a crop that consumes it.

delai.texte: at least 3 years before growing the same crop again, 4 years for potatoes and cassava.

jachere.texte: one season in three, with a cover crop such as Mucuna or Stylosanthes.

association.texte: maize + beans or maize + groundnut on the same plot is acceptable.

jamais.titre: What the tool will never propose
jamais.texte: These sequences are excluded before any score is computed.

manioc.campagne: 1st season (15 March), occupies the whole year

arachide.campagne: Both seasons; too much water at the end rots the pods

pomme_de_terre.campagne: 1st season (in the 2nd, harvesting in the rain causes rot)

exemple.titre: The IRAD plot: a soil that is too acidic
exemple.texte: On the station’s plot, the soil pH is 5.3, below the optimum for all five crops. The tool detects it, still proposes the best-suited rotation (maize, beans, potato, groundnut: 89 out of 100), and adds IRAD’s advice to correct the soil.
exemple.photoAlt: Farm workers in rows of young maize plants
exemple.conseil: Apply 5 to 10 tonnes per hectare of compost or manure, plus wood ash, to raise the pH towards 5.5 to 6.5. For groundnut, ash also supplies the calcium it needs.

pourQui.titre: A tool for those who decide in the field, and those who advise them

agriculteurs.texte: Compare what to plant on their plot, based on what matters to them: yield, water or soil.

techniciens.texte: Back their advice with verified rainfall data and IRAD’s rules, plot by plot.

cooperatives.texte: Plan seeds and growing seasons for their members while accounting for a changing climate.

chercheurs.texte: Test rotation scenarios and compare satellite data with field measurements.

aide.texte: Farmers compare and choose. Proposals should be checked with an extension officer or IRAD.

notes.texte: Scores measure how well crops suit the climate and soil, not a yield in kilograms.

sol.texte: SoilGrids gives an estimate on 250 m squares. A lab soil test is more reliable, and the tool lets farmers enter one.

zone.texte: Data is ready for Dschang and the rules come from IRAD Dschang. Other regions will need their own local rules.

zones.texte: Santchou and the Mbo plain, then other farming basins in Cameroon.

smap.texte: Add NASA SMAP satellite measurements to track the water actually available in the soil.

prevision.texte: A machine learning model to predict the start of the rainy season before planting.

terrain.texte: Test the proposed rotations on IRAD plots and compare harvests.

final.texte: Set your priorities, enter your soil test if you have one, and compare three rotations suited to today’s climate.

equipe.evenement: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 · Yaoundé · “Field Shift” challenge
equipe.merci: Thanks to the researchers of the IRAD Dschang station for their time, their data and their advice.

footer.avertissement: Decision-support tool. Its proposals do not replace the advice of an extension officer.

outil.metaTitre: Field Shift: compare rotations for my plot
outil.intro: Set your priorities on the left: the tool evaluates every possible rotation over 2 years and proposes the three best suited to your plot’s climate and soil.
outil.aucuneZone: No area has data ready yet. Run the data preparation scripts.

rendement.label: Yield
rendement.aide: Crops well suited to the climate and soil

eau.label: Water security
eau.aide: Low risk of running short of water, especially after planting

panneau.precedentAide: The tool avoids planting it again too soon and picks what can follow it.
panneau.analyseSolAide: Otherwise, the tool uses the SoilGrids estimate
panneau.actuelleAide: Enter what you usually grow: the tool scores it with the same criteria as its proposals.

rotations.legende: Scores measure how well crops suit the plot’s climate and soil, not a yield in tonnes. Hatched blocks show the dry season, when the soil is left bare.
rotations.votreRotationAria: Your usual rotation, score {note} out of 100
rotations.ecartPlus: +{n} point compared with your rotation | +{n} points compared with your rotation
rotations.ecartMoins: {n} point below your rotation | {n} points below your rotation

assistant.intro: The assistant explains the results shown, in plain words. It only answers from Field Shift data.
assistant.attente: The assistant is checking the data…

suggestions.acide: My soil is acidic, what should I do?
suggestions.actuelle: Why does my rotation lose points?

assistant.avertissement: Answers written by an AI (Claude, by Anthropic) from Field Shift data only. Every number is checked automatically, but mistakes are still possible: check with an extension officer before deciding.

normes.intro: Every proposed rotation follows these rules: no maize after maize, no beans after groundnut, at least 3 years before the same crop returns (4 years for potatoes and cassava).
